title: Reconcile quota and rate-limit attribution for mixed-cache hybrid batch flows
creator: Ananya Patel
description: Problem: requests that are aggregated into multi-tenant batches or contain a mix of prefix-cache hits, KV cache hits, and live token generation are currently causing incorrect quota accounting and unexpected rate-limit rejections. Observed symptoms include: (1) tenant A receives a 429 even though all generated token cost should be attributed to tenant B in the same fused batch, (2) end-to-end billing overcharges when prefix-cache hits are charged as full input tokens, and (3) burst quotas are consumed unpredictably due to double-counting between prefetch and coalesced batch accounting. This ticket designs and implements a deterministic attribution model and runtime instrumentation to make quota throttling and invoicing correct and explainable.
acceptance_criteria: Metering tags are attached at RPC and batch aggregation boundaries that uniquely identify origin tenant and cache-hit type (prefix, kv, prefetch)
Billing ledger receives per-tenant prorated token entries for fused batches where some requests are cache-hits and some generate tokens
Rate limiter uses predicted generate-token cost rather than naive request-count for mixed-cache batches, avoiding spurious 429s for tenants with only cache-hits
Regression tests cover: pure-prefix-hit, pure-kv-hit, mixed-hit+generate, and multi-tenant fused batches with partial KV hits
Dashboard shows before/after comparison of billed tokens and 429 rate by tenant for a 7-day test window
technical_design: Introduce BatchAttribution object (flat fields only) propagated through serving pipeline: origin_tenant, request_id_list (ids), hit_mask (binary string), predicted_generate_tokens (int), provenance_tag

Change metering pipeline to accept batch-level records and emit per-tenant pro-rated entries: for each batch, compute total_generated_tokens and split token charge by request contribution using predicted_generate_tokens. Cache-hits emit zero generated token charge but still record hit-type event for analytics.

Modify rate limiter hook to consult batch.predicted_generate_tokens for budget checks and to reserve tokens lazily (reservation only for predicted-generated portion) to avoid blocking cache-only requests
Edge-case rule: if a batch contains requests from tenants with shared billing accounts, fallback to account-level aggregation instead of per-tenant split
Add a deterministic tie-breaker for coalesced batches where predicted_generate_tokens are equal (use request arrival ordering) to avoid nondeterministic metering across retries
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): 10% of user traffic routed through metering-v2 path with read-only metering writes (emit metering events to a dry-run topic) — 2 weeks
Phase 2: Enable live per-tenant prorated billing for internal dev accounts and selected pilot customers — 1 week
Phase 3: Full production rollout with monitoring alerts for billing delta > 3% vs legacy pipeline — gated rollout over 48 hours
Rollback: Revert to legacy batch aggregation and mark metering-v2 off in runtime flags if errors exceed threshold
measurement_plan: Key metrics: billed_tokens_by_tenant, 429_rate_by_tenant, billing_delta_percent (v2 vs v1), meter_event_latency
Create dashboard tile comparing per-tenant billed tokens before/after for pilot accounts
Daily job to reconcile metered events to billing ledger and surface any unmatched events within 24h
open_questions: How should we charge for prefix-cache hits that return truncated continuations (do we bill for the part that would have been generated?) — propose zero charge for returned tokens, but log hypothetical charge for analytics
Is it acceptable to prorate non-token charges (e.g., per-request p99 SLO surcharge) across tenants in a fused batch? Recommend not prorating SLO penalties — attribute to origin tenant only
Do we need legal approval to change invoicing semantics for customers on committed tiers? Coordinate with billing/finance

Should prefetch operations that later become cache hits be charged at prefetch time or final request time? Propose charging at prefetch time at a lower prefetch-rate and crediting if served from cache
